commission_settlement_delay.label: Commission confirmed → settled time
commission_settlement_delay.definition: Time between a commission’s confirmation and its settlement being recorded, median and average over settled commissions whose two dates are known.
commission_settlement_delay.excludes: Unsettled commissions; those whose confirmation date is unknown (confirmed before the date was logged) — counted separately, never replaced by a plausible date.
commission_settlement_delay.whenInsufficient: Hidden below 5 observations; the screen says how many are missing.
commission_settlement_delay.howToFeed: One observation = a commission confirmed, then recorded as settled in the tool (Follow-up screen) — each action sets its date.
commission_settlement_delay.filters: Period: on the settlement date. Advisor, type, pipeline and origin: those of the deal as it is today (reassignments are not tracked over time).

commissions_aging.label: Aging of confirmed, unsettled commissions
commissions_aging.definition: Commissions confirmed and not yet settled, by age since confirmation: 0 to 30 days, 31 to 60, 61 to 90, more than 90 — count and amount; plus those beyond the organization’s follow-up threshold (Brand & settings), the same rule as the “commissions to collect” pile in Follow-up.
commissions_aging.excludes: Those whose confirmation date is unknown (confirmed before the date was logged) — counted separately, never given a plausible date.
commissions_aging.howToFeed: Confirm the commission when the deal goes through; record the settlement when it arrives.
commissions_aging.filters: THE PERIOD HAS NO EFFECT (a snapshot as of today). Advisor, type, pipeline, origin: those of the deal.

commissions_outstanding.label: Outstanding commissions by state
commissions_outstanding.definition: All the organization’s commissions, AS OF TODAY, by state: expected (share pending or accepted), confirmed not settled, settled — count and calculated amount — plus expected commissions that lapsed (share declined, revoked, expired or replaced by a resend), counted separately.
commissions_outstanding.excludes: Commissions with no calculated amount, from the sums (counted separately).
commissions_outstanding.howToFeed: Set a commission when sending a share.
commissions_outstanding.filters: THE PERIOD HAS NO EFFECT: an outstanding balance is a snapshot as of today. Advisor, type, pipeline, origin: those of the deal.

creation_to_won.label: Creation → signature time
creation_to_won.definition: Time between the deal’s creation and its FIRST entry into a stage marked “won”, median and average over signed deals.
creation_to_won.excludes: Deals never won; an entry into the won stage reconstructed after the fact; an organization with no stage marked “won” has no measurable signature.
creation_to_won.whenInsufficient: Hidden below 5 observations; the screen says how many are missing.
creation_to_won.howToFeed: One observation = a deal that entered the stage marked “won”.
creation_to_won.filters: Period: on the signature date. Advisor, type, pipeline and origin: those of the deal as it is today (reassignments are not tracked over time).

deals_created.label: Deals created
deals_created.definition: Deals created within the period (creation date) — the same cohort as a pipeline’s funnel, all pipelines combined.
deals_created.excludes: Nothing: a created deal counts, whatever became of it.
deals_created.whenInsufficient: The count is always shown — it’s a fact.
deals_created.howToFeed: Create a deal (contact record, pipeline, “New” menu).
deals_created.filters: Period: on the creation date. Advisor, type, pipeline and origin: those of the deal as it is today (reassignments are not tracked over time).

deals_won.label: Deals signed
deals_won.definition: Deals TODAY in a stage marked “won” whose last entry into that stage falls within the period — the signature date, the same rule as the loss rate and the creation → signature time.
deals_won.excludes: A deal won then reopened (it is no longer won); a signature predating the log (reconstructed row, unknown date) — excluded, never given a plausible date.
deals_won.whenInsufficient: The count is always shown — it’s a fact.
deals_won.howToFeed: Move the deal into the stage marked “won”.
deals_won.filters: Period: on the signature date. Advisor, type, pipeline and origin: those of the deal as it is today (reassignments are not tracked over time).

funnel_by_origin.label: Conversion by origin
funnel_by_origin.definition: The full chain, grouped by origin: visitors, simulations, leads received, contacts made, deals from those leads and deals won — the SAME definitions as the chain, applied to the origin of the event or of the lead. Two rates: lead → deal and deal → won. It answers “which origin generates deals that get signed”.
funnel_by_origin.excludes: Deals with no lead appear on the “no origin” row (deals and won only — nothing upstream corresponds to them). Received texts not attached to a configured origin are grouped under “to match” (Analytics → Origins).
funnel_by_origin.whenInsufficient: Counts are always shown; each rate is hidden below 5 observations in its denominator.
funnel_by_origin.howToFeed: Configure origins and match the received texts (Analytics → Origins); pass the origin in the snippet and in /api/leads.
funnel_by_origin.filters: Those of the chain, step by step; with an origin filter, a single row remains.

funnel_contacted.label: Contacts made
funnel_contacted.definition: Among the leads received within the period, those whose record carries at least one real interaction logged from the lead’s arrival onward — a call, an email or a meeting, not a note — at any date since. Same rule as the lead → first real contact time.
funnel_contacted.excludes: Notes; interactions predating the lead (the relationship already existed); deleted records (their interactions are deleted too). A deal created without a logged interaction does NOT count here: this step measures what is logged. If there are more deals than contacts made, not every interaction is logged — the screen says so.
funnel_contacted.whenInsufficient: The count is always shown — it’s a fact, not a statistic. The conversion rate calculated from this step is hidden while the previous step has fewer than 5 observations.
funnel_contacted.howToFeed: Log a call, an email or a meeting on the record of the contact who came through the lead.
funnel_contacted.filters: The same as “Leads received”: period on the lead’s arrival, the lead’s origin, the record’s advisor.

funnel_conversion_rate.label: Conversion rate and drop-off
funnel_conversion_rate.definition: Between two consecutive steps: the step’s count divided by the previous step’s, in percent; the drop-off is the complement to 100%. A step that is not applicable (a filter that doesn’t apply to it, a source not connected) is skipped: the rate is calculated from the last measurable step.
funnel_conversion_rate.excludes: Nothing is excluded, but a rate can exceed 100% when a step counts more than the previous one — more leads than measured completed simulations (leads arrive without going through the snippet), more deals than contacts made (some interactions are not logged). It isn’t a calculation error, it’s an incomplete measurement upstream: the screen shows it as is and says so, and the drop-off is then not applicable.
funnel_conversion_rate.whenInsufficient: Hidden while the previous step has fewer than 5 observations; the screen says how many are missing. The counts, for their part, stay visible.
funnel_conversion_rate.howToFeed: Feed both steps: the rate appears as soon as the previous step reaches the threshold.
funnel_conversion_rate.filters: Those of the two steps involved.

funnel_deals_from_leads.label: Deals from these leads
funnel_deals_from_leads.definition: Deals whose origin is one of the leads received within the period — a deal’s origin (deals.lead_id) is set at creation from the contact’s latest earlier lead, or attached by hand on the record (logged). A deal counts once; a lead can generate several.
funnel_deals_from_leads.excludes: Deals with no lead (created by hand, unknown origin): the per-pipeline funnel counts them, the chain doesn’t. A lead that arrived AFTER a deal was created is never attached to it on its own.
funnel_deals_from_leads.whenInsufficient: The count is always shown — it’s a fact, not a statistic. The conversion rate calculated from this step is hidden while the previous step has fewer than 5 observations.
funnel_deals_from_leads.howToFeed: Create the deal from the record of a contact who came through a lead (the origin is set on its own), or attach the lead on the deal record.
funnel_deals_from_leads.filters: Period: on the LEAD’S ARRIVAL, not on the deal’s creation (the chain follows the period’s leads up to today). Advisor, type, pipeline and origin: those of the deal as it is today (reassignments are not tracked over time).

funnel_leads.label: Leads received
funnel_leads.definition: Leads recorded by the server endpoint (POST /api/leads) within the period — one arrival per lead, even when several come from the same person. This is the step where the chain moves from an anonymous browser to a person: the upstream steps count browsers, this one and the following ones count leads and deals.
funnel_leads.excludes: Submissions rejected by the API (missing or revoked key, invalid payload, rate limit exceeded): they are not recorded — Brand & settings → Capture counts them separately.
funnel_leads.whenInsufficient: The count is always shown — it’s a fact, not a statistic. The conversion rate calculated from this step is hidden while the previous step has fewer than 5 observations. As long as no lead has ever been received, the step is “not connected yet”.
funnel_leads.howToFeed: Have the simulator or the site call POST /api/leads with an API key (Brand & settings → Capture).
funnel_leads.filters: Period: on the lead’s arrival. Origin: the lead’s. Advisor: the one on the lead’s contact record. Type and pipeline: no effect here — they only apply from deals onward.

funnel_simulations_completed.label: Simulations completed
funnel_simulations_completed.definition: Distinct browsers for which the snippet received “simulation completed” within the period. Several completed simulations from the same browser count once.
funnel_simulations_completed.excludes: Simulators that don’t emit the signal. A completed simulation declared only on the lead (dates passed by the simulator’s server) is not a visit event: it lives on the lead, not here.
funnel_simulations_completed.whenInsufficient: The count is always shown — it’s a fact, not a statistic. The conversion rate calculated from this step is hidden while the previous step has fewer than 5 observations.
funnel_simulations_completed.howToFeed: Call clozado.track("simulation_completed") at the simulator’s last step.
funnel_simulations_completed.filters: Period: on the event. Origin: the one passed by the page (attached to a configured origin, or “to match”). Advisor: not applicable — a visit is not attached to anyone; with this filter, the step is not applicable. Type and pipeline: no effect (nothing is a deal yet).

funnel_simulations_started.label: Simulations started
funnel_simulations_started.definition: Distinct browsers for which the snippet received “simulation started” within the period — a signal the simulator emits itself (clozado.track). Several simulations from the same browser count once.
funnel_simulations_started.excludes: Simulators that don’t emit the signal; a simulation started outside the period.
funnel_simulations_started.whenInsufficient: The count is always shown — it’s a fact, not a statistic. The conversion rate calculated from this step is hidden while the previous step has fewer than 5 observations.
funnel_simulations_started.howToFeed: Call clozado.track("simulation_started") at the simulator’s first step (Brand & settings → Capture shows the snippet and how to use it).
funnel_simulations_started.filters: Period: on the event. Origin: the one passed by the page (attached to a configured origin, or “to match”). Advisor: not applicable — a visit is not attached to anyone; with this filter, the step is not applicable. Type and pipeline: no effect (nothing is a deal yet).

funnel_stage_leak.label: Drop-off at a stage: lost and open
funnel_stage_leak.definition: The cohort’s deals that reached the stage without reaching the next one — either LOST (today in a stage marked “lost”, counted at the furthest stage they reached), or OPEN (furthest in this stage, still open today, even if they have moved back since). Lost + open = everything missing from the next step.
funnel_stage_leak.excludes: Won deals (they are missing from no step).
funnel_stage_leak.whenInsufficient: The count is always shown — it’s a fact, not a statistic. The conversion rate calculated from this step is hidden while the previous step has fewer than 5 observations.
funnel_stage_leak.howToFeed: Moving a deal into the stage marked “lost” (with its reason) files it here, at the stage it had reached.
funnel_stage_leak.filters: The same as “Deals that reached a stage”.

funnel_stage_reached.label: Deals that reached a stage
funnel_stage_reached.definition: Among the deals CREATED within the period (a cohort, followed up to today), those that entered the stage or a more advanced stage of the same pipeline, or that are won today: a deal that went straight from the first to the third stage has reached the second — it went at least that far. The first stage counts every deal created.
funnel_stage_reached.excludes: Nothing: an entry reconstructed after the fact counts too — what matters here is having entered, not the date. The final stages (won, lost) are not funnel steps: won is the finish line, lost is the drop-off.
funnel_stage_reached.whenInsufficient: The count is always shown — it’s a fact, not a statistic. The conversion rate calculated from this step is hidden while the previous step has fewer than 5 observations.
funnel_stage_reached.howToFeed: Create deals and move them forward stage by stage (kanban or record).
funnel_stage_reached.filters: Period: on the deal’s CREATION (cohort). Advisor, type, pipeline and origin: those of the deal as it is today (reassignments are not tracked over time). One funnel per pipeline.

funnel_visitors.label: Visitors
funnel_visitors.definition: Distinct browsers (the anonymous identifier set by the JavaScript snippet, never an IP address) that loaded a page carrying the snippet within the period. The same browser coming back counts once.
funnel_visitors.excludes: Pages without the snippet; browsers that refuse all storage (no identifier, hence no visit); submissions rejected by the API (undeclared domain, revoked key) — counted in Brand & settings → Capture, never here.
funnel_visitors.whenInsufficient: The count is always shown — it’s a fact, not a statistic. The conversion rate calculated from this step is hidden while the previous step has fewer than 5 observations. As long as no visit has ever been received, the step is “not connected yet”.
funnel_visitors.howToFeed: Install the JavaScript snippet on the site (Brand & settings → Capture): every load of a page carrying it counts.
funnel_visitors.filters: Period: on the event. Origin: the one passed by the page (attached to a configured origin, or “to match”). Advisor: not applicable — a visit is not attached to anyone; with this filter, the step is not applicable. Type and pipeline: no effect (nothing is a deal yet).

funnel_won.label: Deals won
funnel_won.definition: Among the previous step’s deals, those that are TODAY in a stage marked “won” — the current state, the one on the kanban. In the chain, the previous step is “deals from these leads”; in a pipeline’s funnel, the last intermediate stage.
funnel_won.excludes: A deal won then moved out of the stage (reopened) is no longer won; an organization with no stage marked “won” has no measurable signature.
funnel_won.whenInsufficient: The count is always shown — it’s a fact, not a statistic. The conversion rate calculated from this step is hidden while the previous step has fewer than 5 observations.
funnel_won.howToFeed: Move the deal into the stage marked “won” (kanban or record).
funnel_won.filters: The same as the previous step. Advisor, type, pipeline and origin: those of the deal as it is today (reassignments are not tracked over time).

lead_to_first_contact.label: Lead → first real contact time
lead_to_first_contact.definition: For each contact who came through a lead, time between the arrival of their FIRST lead and the first interaction logged with them from then on (a call, an email or a meeting — not a note), median and average.
lead_to_first_contact.excludes: Contacts with no interaction logged since the lead’s arrival (counted separately: they are still waiting for a first contact); notes (a note is not a contact); interactions predating the lead (the relationship already existed); contacts who arrived other than through a lead; deleted records (their interactions are deleted too).
lead_to_first_contact.whenInsufficient: Hidden below 5 observations; the screen says how many are missing.
lead_to_first_contact.howToFeed: One observation = a lead received through the API (Brand & settings → Capture), then a call, an email or a meeting logged on the contact’s record.
lead_to_first_contact.filters: Period: on the first interaction. Advisor: the one on the contact record. Origin: the first lead’s. Deal type and pipeline: no effect — this time is measured before any deal exists.

loss_breakdown.label: Loss breakdown
loss_breakdown.definition: The period’s lost deals, broken down by reason (at the time of the loss), by starting stage (the one the deal fell from — “from creation” if it was born lost), by advisor in charge and by deal type; for each row, the count, the amount lost and the proportion of the total.
loss_breakdown.excludes: The same as “Deals lost”. A deal lost without a reason appears on the “No reason” row — a piece of information, not an oversight in the calculation.
loss_breakdown.whenInsufficient: A row’s proportion is hidden while total losses are below 5; counts and amounts are always shown.
loss_breakdown.howToFeed: Configure the reasons (Brand & settings) and pick the reason at the time of the loss.
loss_breakdown.filters: The same as “Deals lost”; each row opens the list of the deals it counts.

loss_rate.label: Loss rate
loss_rate.definition: Over the period, lost deals as a proportion of closed deals (lost + won) — won by the same rule: today in a stage marked “won”, at the date of their last entry into that stage.
loss_rate.excludes: Deals still open (not closed); reconstructed entries, on both sides.
loss_rate.whenInsufficient: Hidden below 5 closed deals; the screen says how many are missing.

lost_deal.label: Deals lost
lost_deal.definition: A deal TODAY in a stage marked “lost” (the current state, the one on the kanban). Its loss date, starting stage and reason are those of its LAST entry into the lost stage, read from the stage-change log — the reason at the time of the loss, not the record’s current value. The amount lost is the deal’s estimated amount (current value).
lost_deal.excludes: A deal lost then reopened (it is alive). A loss predating the log — its entry row was reconstructed at the creation date, the actual loss date is unknown: excluded from the calculation and counted separately, never given a plausible date. Deals with no estimated amount count in the count, not in the amount — counted separately.
lost_deal.whenInsufficient: Counts and amounts are always shown; only the proportions (in percent) are hidden below 5 losses.
lost_deal.howToFeed: Move a deal into the stage marked “lost” and pick its reason (kanban or record) — the reason can be corrected on the record as long as the deal stays there.
lost_deal.filters: Period: on the loss date (last entry into the lost stage). Advisor, type, pipeline and origin: those of the deal as it is today (reassignments are not tracked over time).

partner_acceptance_rate.label: Acceptance rate
partner_acceptance_rate.definition: Per partner, accepted shares as a proportion of shares sent — a share with no response is not accepted. Declined and no response are shown alongside.
partner_acceptance_rate.whenInsufficient: Hidden while the partner has fewer than 5 shares sent.
partner_acceptance_rate.howToFeed: The partner responds from their link (accept, decline).

partner_commissions.label: Commissions generated
partner_commissions.definition: Per partner, on the period’s shares: EARNED commissions (confirmed or settled, at the calculated amount frozen at confirmation) and EXPECTED commissions still alive (share pending or accepted). A chain of resends carries a single commission: the one on its last link.
partner_commissions.excludes: Expected commissions of a share that was declined, revoked, expired or replaced by a resend (lapsed); a commission with no calculated amount counts in the count, not in the sum — counted separately.
partner_commissions.howToFeed: Set the commission when sending the share, confirm it when the deal goes through, record its settlement (Follow-up screen).

partner_response_delay.label: Partner response time
partner_response_delay.definition: Per partner, the same measure as “Share → partner response time” on the Timings screen: from the chain’s first send to the response (acceptance or decline), median and average.
partner_response_delay.excludes: Shares with no response; links replaced by a resend (only the last one carries the response).
partner_response_delay.whenInsufficient: Hidden below 5 observations; the screen says how many are missing.
partner_response_delay.howToFeed: One observation = a share the partner responded to.
partner_response_delay.filters: Period: on the first send (the cohort), not on the response — the Timings screen, for its part, bounds on the response date. Advisor, type, pipeline, origin: those of the deal.

partner_shares.label: Shares sent
partner_shares.definition: Per partner, the shares sent within the period, followed up to today. A share = a chain of link resends: the resent link is not a second share, it’s the same one, sent on the date of the first, and only the last link in the chain carries the response and the commission. A share’s outcome is that of its last link: accepted, declined, or no response (pending, expired, revoked).
partner_shares.excludes: Nothing: a share revoked without a response counts as no response, not as declined.
partner_shares.whenInsufficient: The count is always shown — it’s a fact, not a statistic. The conversion rate calculated from this step is hidden while the previous step has fewer than 5 observations.
partner_shares.howToFeed: Share a deal from its record.
partner_shares.filters: Period: on the chain’s FIRST send (the cohort). Advisor, type, pipeline and origin: those of the deal as it is today (reassignments are not tracked over time).

partner_transformation_rate.label: Win rate
partner_transformation_rate.definition: Per partner, among accepted shares, those whose deal is TODAY in a stage marked “won” (current state), as a proportion of accepted shares.
partner_transformation_rate.excludes: Shares not accepted; a deal won then reopened is no longer won.
partner_transformation_rate.whenInsufficient: Hidden while the partner has fewer than 5 accepted shares.
partner_transformation_rate.howToFeed: Move the shared deal into the stage marked “won”.

pipeline_open.label: Open deals
pipeline_open.definition: AS OF TODAY, the deals in a stage with no outcome (neither won nor lost) and the sum of their estimated amounts — the open pipeline value, what can still be signed.
pipeline_open.excludes: Deals with no estimated amount, from the sum (counted separately); closed deals.
pipeline_open.whenInsufficient: The count and the amount are always shown.
pipeline_open.howToFeed: Create deals and move them forward in the pipeline.
pipeline_open.filters: THE PERIOD HAS NO EFFECT: open pipeline value is a snapshot as of today. Advisor, type, pipeline, origin: those of the deal.

share_response_delay.label: Share → partner response time
share_response_delay.definition: Time between a share being sent and the partner’s response (acceptance or decline). A resent link doesn’t count as a new share: the time starts from the chain’s FIRST send.
share_response_delay.excludes: Shares with no response (pending, revoked without a response, expired); shares replaced by a resend (only the last one in the chain carries the response).
share_response_delay.whenInsufficient: Hidden below 5 observations; the screen says how many are missing.
share_response_delay.howToFeed: One observation = a share the partner responded to from their link (accepted or declined).
share_response_delay.filters: Period: on the response date. Advisor, type, pipeline and origin: those of the deal as it is today (reassignments are not tracked over time).

stage_duration.label: Time in stage
stage_duration.definition: For each intermediate stage of the pipeline, time between a deal entering the stage and leaving it (the next stage change), median and average over completed stays. A deal that revisits a stage counts one stay per visit.
stage_duration.excludes: The current stay (the deal is still there — counted separately); rows reconstructed after the fact (initial stage row deduced from the creation date) — counted separately, never in the duration; the final stages (won, lost): a deal doesn’t leave them, so the time spent there measures nothing.
stage_duration.whenInsufficient: Hidden below 5 observations; the screen says how many are missing.
stage_duration.howToFeed: One observation = a completed stay: moving a deal to another stage (kanban or record) closes the previous stay.
stage_duration.filters: Period: on the end of the stay. Advisor, type, pipeline and origin: those of the deal as it is today (reassignments are not tracked over time).

stage_pair_delay.label: Time between two consecutive stages
stage_pair_delay.definition: For each pair of successive stages in a pipeline, time between a deal’s first entry into the first and its first entry into the second, over deals that reached both — median and average.
stage_pair_delay.excludes: Deals that didn’t reach the second stage; non-consecutive pairs; reconstructed entries; pairs that would start from a final stage (won, lost): it has no next stage.
stage_pair_delay.whenInsufficient: Hidden below 5 observations; the screen says how many are missing.
stage_pair_delay.howToFeed: One observation = a deal that entered the first stage, then the second.
stage_pair_delay.filters: Period: on the entry into the second stage. Advisor, type, pipeline and origin: those of the deal as it is today (reassignments are not tracked over time).

won_amount.label: Signed amount
won_amount.definition: The sum of the estimated amounts of the period’s signed deals (“Deals signed”, same rule) — a wealth advisor’s inflows, a broker’s volume. The deal’s estimated amount, current value, by design.
won_amount.excludes: Signed deals with no estimated amount: in the count, not in the sum — counted separately, and an amount about which nothing is known is written “—”, never €0.
won_amount.howToFeed: Fill in the estimated amount on the deal record.

assurance.label: Insurance broker
assurance.audience: Borrower insurance, protection, health, property and casualty.
assurance.description: Conversion and responsiveness: leads received and time to first contact, cases created and signed, what gets lost and why, share acceptance, earned commissions.
